title: VA Home Loan Guaranty Relief for Deed in Lieu and Compromise Sale Liquidations
content:
On a liquidated VA Home Loan Guaranty loan, the amount of entitlement held back against the unrecovered guaranty loss is reduced according to the way the loan was liquidated, as the liquidation type on the guaranty claim entry in the loan's money transactions shows it.

## Relief by liquidation type

| The guaranty claim paid on the loan followed | Reduction of the amount held back |
|---|---|
| A deed in lieu | 30 percent |
| A compromise sale | 15 percent |
| A foreclosure sale | No reduction for the way the loan was liquidated (0 percent) |

Where more than one guaranty claim entry appears, the liquidation type read is that of the latest one.

## Worked figures (hypothetical amount held back of 20,000.00 dollars)

| Liquidation type on the claim | Reduction | Amount after the reduction |
|---|---|---|
| Deed in lieu | 30 | 20,000.00 times one minus 30 divided by one hundred, or 14,000.00 |
| Compromise sale | 15 | 20,000.00 times one minus 15 divided by one hundred, or 17,000.00 |
| Foreclosure sale | 0 | 20,000.00 |

## Basis questions

**Does a compromise sale receive the same relief as a deed in lieu?** No. A deed in lieu carries 30 percent and a compromise sale 15 percent.

**Is anything reduced for a foreclosure sale?** No reduction applies for the way the loan was liquidated where the claim followed a foreclosure sale.
